title: Coded titles and the clique of 'regular' musicians
summary: Bands hid titles to stop theft; Scott explains that regular musicians in the clique got the best jobs.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yes, well, didn't some bands not have the title on the music, used numbers and stuff to make it more difficult?

Yes, yes, because they stole it. So that's what they used to do. Well, sometimes I had to go with the fellows I was working with, because after all, that was the difference with musicians. You were either regular or you weren't.
Now, the regular guys, they got jobs and got work. The guys that wasn't regular they didn't bother with. So they didn't call them, they didn't get work. Had to be regular.
And regular meant -- what? What did regular mean?
They were in the clique. They called it a clique, be in the know. See, I was in the clique because I had worked with Fletcher and Duke. And then they put me in a clique, those fellows' names, see.

But if you wasn't in the clique, you didn't get that much work. You didn't get any work. You had to take what's left. The clique got the best of the jobs and what's left they got. Well, that's the way it was, that's the way it was. And it was natural.
So I think I'm a little ahead of my -- oh, no, I'm not.
